$ filo indexes (none yet)
Indexes   none yet

Next: filo indexes add [DIR] [--name NAME] writes the pages of a directory's files by tag

$ filo indexes add received
Index added   received/index.html . 2 files . 2 tags . 5 pages . <root>
  - its pages are in received/.index/; scans skip both

Next: open <root>/received/index.html in a browser

$ filo indexes add . --name tags (the root)
Index added   tags.html . 3 files . 2 tags . 8 pages . <root>
  - its pages are in .tags/; scans skip both
  - 1 file has no tags: it is listed on the page "no tags"

Next: open <root>/tags.html in a browser

$ filo indexes
Indexes   2 . <root>

  tags.html             3 files   2 tags   written 2026-11-22 12:00
  received/index.html   2 files   2 tags   written 2026-11-22 12:00

Next: open an index's page in a browser

$ filo indexes (one flagged)
Indexes   2 . 1 needs attention . <root>

  tags.html             3 files   3 tags   written 2026-11-22 12:00
  received/index.html   2 files   3 tags   written 2026-11-22 12:00   [!] not up to date
    [!] received/index.html was changed since Filo wrote it: not replaced

Next: move aside what is flagged, then filo indexes refresh <root>/received

$ filo indexes refresh
Refreshed   2 indexes . <root>
  - tags.html             up to date
  [ok] received/index.html   1 page written

$ filo indexes remove . --name tags

    tags.html
    .tags/      9 files: its pages and style.css
  [!] .tags/notes.txt is not Filo's: it stays, and so does .tags/

Remove the index and its 10 files? [y/N] 
Done   removed 10 files
  [!] .tags holds files that are not Filo's: it stays

$ filo indexes remove received
